intro: If you want a place in central Sa Kaeo with a pool to cool off in, spacious rooms, and an easy walk to the train station and market, Thanasiri Hotel & Resort is a name self-drivers and train travellers come back to · It sits on Thetsaban 19 Road, about 200 m from Sa Kaeo railway station and roughly a 10-minute walk to the town centre · Rooms are spacious, some with a small kitchenette and fridge, and there's an outdoor pool, free parking, free Wi-Fi and a 24-hour front desk · Rooms start from around ฿750/night, an easy way to get both a pool and a central location at a price that stays grounded.

body.html: Thanasiri Hotel & Resort sits at 144/2 Thetsaban 19 Road in Mueang Sa Kaeo district — a town hotel only about 200 m from Sa Kaeo railway station and a roughly 10-minute walk from the town centre · That location makes it an easy overnight stop for both self-drivers and people arriving by train, close to the market and the Chao Por Sa Kaeo shrine, with food within walking distance in the evening.

What guests mention most is that the rooms are big and clean, and the hotel has a swimming pool — an advantage over many in-town options in Sa Kaeo that have no pool at all · Several reviews say the rooms are larger than expected, the beds are comfortable, and you get air-conditioning, a fridge, satellite TV, and in some rooms a small kitchenette with a microwave, which suits longer stays or anyone who wants to heat up their own food · Wi-Fi is in every room and the overall feel is quiet, with good sleep.
"Big, clean room, central location near the train station and market, staff who smiled a lot, and we slept very well — good value for an overnight stop in Sa Kaeo town."

Another thing guests praise is that most of the staff are friendly and smiley, especially the breakfast team · There's an on-site restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and dinner, plus room service, a coffee shop, and a karaoke/game room to unwind · For self-drivers there is free parking on site and a 24-hour front desk, handy for late arrivals into town.

To be honest about the weak points — breakfast is fairly basic · some reviews note only a couple of options and a few items served cold, not the big buffet some people expect · The recurring niggles are noisy air-conditioning in some rooms that cycles on and off and can interrupt sleep, a few rooms being on the dark side with only a small window, and Wi-Fi that can be patchy at times · There are also reviews mentioning unexpected charges at checkout (such as for towels) and reception staff who weren't always welcoming, so it's worth confirming the details up front.

Bottom line: Thanasiri Hotel & Resort suits anyone who wants a central Sa Kaeo hotel with a pool, big rooms, and an easy walk to the train station and market at a grounded price — good for an overnight stop on the way to Aranyaprathet and the Rong Kluea border market, or for errands in town · An overall score around 8.0 from real reviews reflects exactly that — spacious rooms, a pool, a good location, but a basic breakfast and service that can be uneven · Set expectations accordingly, confirm any charges in advance, and most people get a comfortable night here.

honestSummary: Thanasiri Hotel & Resort is a central Sa Kaeo option that gives you a pool, big rooms, and a location near the train station and market at a grounded price — handy for self-drivers and train travellers · The trade-off is a basic breakfast and service that can be uneven.
honestChecks: If you want a town hotel with a pool — this delivers: big rooms, a pool, a location near the station → just don't expect a luxury resort or a large pool.
If you expect a buffet breakfast — it's served simply here, with few options and some items cold → plan on a spot in Sa Kaeo town for breakfast.
If you're a light sleeper — the air-con in some rooms is noisy when it cycles, and a few rooms are dark with small windows → ask to switch rooms at check-in and confirm any charges before you pay.

tips.title: Ask for a brighter room with quiet air-con
tips.body: Some rooms have only a small window and are on the dark side, and the air-con can be noisy when it cycles. Ask for a room with natural light and check the air-con is quiet at check-in for a better night's sleep.

tips.title: Confirm any charges up front
tips.body: Some reviews mention unexpected charges at checkout, such as for towels. Ask about anything extra at check-in so there are no surprises.

tips.title: Keep a town eatery in reserve
tips.body: Breakfast is basic with few options, but the hotel is close to the market and town centre, so food for morning or evening is an easy walk away.

tips.title: Use it as a base for Rong Kluea Market
tips.body: Stay in Sa Kaeo town and drive on to Aranyaprathet, the Rong Kluea border market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint — a handy overnight stop before the border.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Thanasiri Hotel & Resort Sa Kaeo

faq.q: Where is Thanasiri Hotel & Resort in Sa Kaeo?
faq.a: It's at 144/2 Thetsaban 19 Road in Mueang Sa Kaeo district, in the town centre · about 200 m from Sa Kaeo railway station and roughly a 10-minute walk to the centre, near the market and the Chao Por Sa Kaeo shrine · easy to drive on from here to Aranyaprathet and the Rong Kluea market.

faq.q: What's the starting price and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around ฿750/night for a Superior · there's a King Deluxe around ฿950 and a Deluxe with kitchenette from about ฿1,200 · prices depend on the season and can climb to roughly ฿1,400–1,500 at peak times, so compare a few platforms before booking.
Yes, there's an outdoor swimming pool — an advantage over many in-town Sa Kaeo hotels that have no pool · there's also a spa, restaurant, coffee shop, and a karaoke/game room to unwind.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they spacious?
faq.a: The strong point is that rooms are big, clean and the beds are comfortable, larger than expected for the price, with air-con, fridge, satellite TV, and in some rooms a small kitchenette with microwave — good for longer stays · note that a few rooms are dark with only a small window, and the air-con can be noisy when it cycles.

Breakfast is fairly basic — some reviews note few options and a few items served cold, not a big buffet · the hotel is close to the market and town centre, so finding breakfast nearby is an easy walk.

faq.q: Who is this hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone who wants a central Sa Kaeo hotel with a pool, big rooms, and an easy walk to the station and market at a grounded price, for an overnight stop or errands in town · one thing to know — confirm any charges before you pay, as some reviews report extra charges at checkout.
